newsitem.title: INDIA: India hit by second mild earthquake in 48 hours.
newsitem.headline: India hit by second mild earthquake in 48 hours.

text.p: The second mild earthquake in less than 48 hours shook India on Tuesday but there were no reports of injuries or damage, officials said.
The Indian Meteorological Department said the tremor, which measured 4.8 on the Richter scale, struck the northeastern state of Assam at 5:42 a.m. (0012 GMT).
Its epicentre was in Cachar district, about 300 km (180 miles) southwest of the state capital Guwahati, the department said.
Late on Sunday, an earthquake also measuring 4.8 on the Richter scale struck the western state of Gujarat.
In 1993, a quake measuring 6.4 on the Richter scale devastated a large area of neighbouring Maharashtra state, killing between 10,000 and 22,000 people and leaving about 150,000 homeless.
Earthquakes between four and five on the Richter scale are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in a populated area.
